messages.subject: Fwd: [GSoC Mentors Announce] Google Code-in 2014 Org application period now open
parts:
Dear R-GSOC mentors,

Brian and I went to the GSOC mentor summit this weekend in San Jose. We were invited to submit an application for the R project to participate in the Google Code-In. It is similar to the GSOC, but with high school students, and smaller, more well-defined tasks (like writing tests and documentation for packages). Below is a message from the Google Code-In admins, with more information. Is there anyone who is willing to step up and volunteer as an Admin for the R project's participation in the Google Code In? I unfortunately do not have the time this year.


---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Google Summer of Code Mentors Announce List <gsoc-mento...@googlegroups.com>
Date: Tue, Oct 28, 2014 at 1:36 AM
Subject: [GSoC Mentors Announce] Google Code-in 2014 Org application period now open
To: gsoc-mento...@googlegroups.com


Hello GSoC Mentors and aspiring GCI Org Admins,


Earlier today we opened the Google Code-in 2014 Mentoring Org app. Organizations that would like to apply for GCI 2014 can submit their application from today until Monday, November 10th at 19:00 UTC. You can now go to the contest site [0] and Register as an Org Admin. Once you have created your Org Admin profile you can go back to the homepage and the Mentoring Org app button will appear for you.


This year we will have 10-12 open source organizations work with the students as mentoring orgs. All organizations that have participated in a previous Google Summer of Code are eligible to apply. This is not like GSoC, we do not get hundreds of applications from orgs so don't be scared away by the relatively low number of orgs. The main thing that we are looking for are orgs that can be patient with the students and who are interested in helping 13-17 year olds learn about open source development.


For some general tips about mentoring for GCI and what to expect you can check out the new GCI Mentor info [1].


Important Upcoming Dates:

** Monday, November 10, 2014 at 17:00 UTC - DEADLINE for orgs to apply as Mentoring Orgs for Google Code-in 2014.


November 12, 2014 - The 10-12 Mentoring organizations are announced for Google Code-in 2014 and the orgs can start entering their tasks into the Google system (the tasks will not be viewable to students until the contest opens on Dec 1).


December 1, 2014 19:00 UTC - Google Code-in 2014 contest opens for students


January 19, 2015 17:00 UTC - Google Code-in 2014 student work ends


January 21, 2015 17:00 UTC - Deadline for Mentors to evaluate student work


January 26, 2015 - Mentoring Organization deadline for submitting their 2 Grand Prize Winners


We hope you will help us spread the word about the Google Code-in contest so we can introduce more young developers to the wonderful world of open source.  If you will be going to any talks or conferences aimed at pre-university students in the next month we would be happy to send you some cool GCI 2014 stickers. Please contact me directly at stta...@google.com if you would like stickers or if you have any questions about applying to be a mentoring organization.


[0]  http://www.google-melange.com/gci/homepage/google/gci2014

[1] https://developers.google.com/open-source/gci/resources/mentor-and-orgadmin-info


Thanks,


Stephanie Taylor

Google Code-in 2014 Program Manager

messages.author: 91d503f5958d266c
messages.subject: Re: [GSoC Mentors Announce] Google Code-in 2014 Org application period now open
parts:
Dear Gaurav, thanks for volunteering to administer the R project's participation in Google Code-in. Please prepare an application!

Usually it is good to have a co-administrator... do you know anyone else who could help you with the admin duties? Again I'm sorry but I probably won't have time to commit to being an admin for GCI this year.

Also after talking to some others who have participated in GCI in previous years, it seems like you need to find mentors who can commit a lot of time to helping the GCI students, especially in the first weeks of student coding (during which there are many eager students who need technical advice). I guess you could start by asking GSOC mentors if they want to participate in GCI.

Finally I think you should set up a wiki page with a table for possible GCI projects (like we had for GSOC on the RWiki http://rwiki.sciviews.org/doku.php?id=developers:projects:gsoc2014). However the Rwiki is down so perhaps you could create a new GSOC/GCI-R group and wiki page on GitHub?
